Kakheti Wine Loop

Three days across the Alazani valley: Sighnaghi, Bodbe, Telavi, Tsinandali, Alaverdi and Kvareli.

days
3 / 2 nights
Total distance
420 km
Total driving
8:00
Car needed
Economy class

All year
Difficulty
Easy

Click a marker for details. Coloured lines are ready-made road trips.

Kakheti is the heart of Georgian wine and the easiest region in the country to drive. The whole loop is on asphalt, the legs between stops are short, and you are never more than two hours from Tbilisi. Three days is what it takes to stop rushing through cellars and instead sit down, taste properly and sleep where you tasted.

Day one belongs to Sighnaghi, the walled hill town whose cobbled lanes and rampart walk frame the Alazani valley and the whole Caucasus ridge in a single view; two kilometres away is Bodbe Monastery, the burial place of St Nino. Day two is the regional capital, Telavi, with the Batonis Tsikhe palace of King Erekle II, followed by Tsinandali — the Chavchavadze estate with its English-style garden and the 1841 cellar that produced Georgia's first bottled wine. Day three opens with Alaverdi, a fifty-metre eleventh-century cathedral standing alone in the fields, and ends in the Kindzmarauli zone around Kvareli.

What you actually see: qvevri cellars where wine ferments in buried clay jars, family tables that turn into long lunches, endless vineyards under the mountains, and several of the greatest monuments of Georgian architecture. The route works all year, but late September and October, during the rtveli harvest, is unbeatable. An economy car is entirely enough. One rule matters above all: whoever drives does not taste.

Day-by-day plan

Day 1 · Tbilisi → Sighnaghi (115 km, 2 h) - 09:30 Leave Tbilisi on the Kakheti highway, coffee stop near Sagarejo. - 11:30 Arrive Sighnaghi and check in. - 12:30 Lunch, then the cobbled centre, the town wall and the valley view (2 h). - 15:30 Bodbe Monastery and the spring of St Nino (1 h 30 min). - 18:00 Tasting at a family cellar in Sighnaghi or Bodbe. - Overnight in Sighnaghi.

Day 2 · Sighnaghi → Telavi (60 km, 1 h 15 min) - 10:00 Drive via Tsnori and Gurjaani with views over the Alazani valley. - 11:30 Telavi: Batonis Tsikhe, the royal palace and the 900-year-old plane tree (2 h). - 14:00 Lunch near the Telavi market (1 h). - 16:00 The two Shuamta monasteries or a walk through town (1 h 30 min). - 19:00 Dinner with a tasting; overnight in Telavi.

Day 3 · Telavi → Tsinandali → Alaverdi → Kvareli → Tbilisi (215 km, 4 h 15 min) - 09:00 Tsinandali estate, garden and historic cellar (2 h). - 11:30 Alaverdi Cathedral (1 h). - 13:30 Kvareli: the Kindzmarauli winery and the wine tunnels (2 h). - 15:30 Late lunch in Kvareli or by Ilia Lake (1 h). - 17:00 Return via Gurjaani and Sagarejo. - 20:00 Back in Tbilisi.

Stops on this route

Town

Sighnaghi

A small walled town on a ridge above the Alazani Valley, with the most photographed view in Kakheti.

3 h
Monastery

Bodbe Monastery

The burial place of St Nino beside Sighnaghi — one of Kakheti's most visited shrines, with a cypress avenue and valley views.

2 h
Town

Telavi and Batonis Tsikhe

The capital of Kakheti on a terrace above the Alazani Valley, with King Erekle II's residence and a nine-century-old plane tree.

3 h
Museum

Tsinandali Estate

The Chavchavadze family house, a landscaped English-style park and the first European-style winery in Georgia.

2 h
Monastery

Alaverdi Cathedral

An eleventh-century cathedral rising fifty metres out of the Alazani plain — for centuries the tallest building in Georgia.

1 h
Winery

Kvareli and the Kindzmarauli zone

Kakheti's main red-wine microzone — tunnel cellars cut into rock, two lakes and a natural base for a harvest trip.

4 h

Tips

  • The driver does not taste — Georgia enforces a zero alcohol limit; agree in advance who drives each day.
  • The rtveli harvest runs from late September through October: the best time for cellars, and the time hotels fill first.
  • Call small family cellars ahead — many receive guests by appointment only.
  • Alaverdi and Bodbe have a dress code; scarves and wraps are usually available at the gate.
  • Leave boot space for bottles, and pack them upright and padded for the drive home.
